newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela's Amuay refinery lifts heavy crude use.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela's Amuay refinery lifts heavy crude use.

text.p: Venezuela's 620,000 barrel per day (bpd) Amuay refinery increased its heavy crude throughput by 17 percent in 1996 to 125,000 bpd, state oil susidiary Lagoven said in a statement on Monday.

Lagoven, a subsidiary of state-owned PDVSA, said total capacity utilisation rose by just two percent to 485,000 bpd, but the heavy crude element rose to one quarter of this figure. In 1997, the company hopes heavy crude throughput will rise again from 125,000 bpd to 139,000 bpd.
PDVSA has a policy of increasing its heavy crude processing because 70 percent of its 66 billion barrels of proven reserves are heavy.
Amuay's statement made no mention of a month-long shutdown of its 100,000 bpd catalytic cracker in October 1996 which had a significant impact on worldwide gasoline markets.
Amuay's refinery manager Heraldo Sifontes said the refinery raised its alkylation unit capacity to 2,000 bpd in 1996 and a 2,000 tonne per year sulphur recovery unit began operation.
